facts.text: The climbers' turnoff is marked with pink flagging, roughly 1.5 miles up the valley trail; overshooting it ends at a creek crossing, so turn uphill early.
In mid-June the lowest heather ledges had melted out while higher ones kept a steep snow ramp; the low line runs close to the cliff edge.
In early July two stretches of the high glacier line lie under rockfall chutes; loose blocks had already landed on the snow.
By late July the bergschrund is widening high on the glacier and moats are opening along the rock; choose the approach line to the saddle with care.
Glacier condition swings by year: in mid-August 2026 it was easy enough to cross unroped, while another year in the same fortnight showed large open crevasses.
Fill bottles at the meadow streams and the glacier edge: by late July nothing flows above the glacier, and 1-1.5 L covered the day for one party.
The high camp near 5,900 ft above the pass has room for only about four tents in mid-July; arrive early or plan to share.
Long trousers and sleeves for brush and blowdowns (June-July)

Most parties now come in by the Bedal Creek trail instead: the road up to it is potholed with one washed-out stretch near the top, so bring high clearance, and from the upper parking head straight into the forest rather than up the logging spur to the right (in early July the first mile is choked with blowdown and brush).

notes: Our stored Corkscrew approach text describes the North Fork Sauk / Cougar Creek approach from FR 49, but the stored trailhead pin and every complete recorded trip use the Bedal Creek trailhead; the approach text and pin disagree (most recent reports are Bedal Creek). The Corkscrew route already holds track points (153); tracks 3385797 (Aug 16 2026, logged Corkscrew Route) and 2605235 (Aug 10 2024) are equally good alternates. Fire on the Mountain, NW Buttress, Diamond in the Rough: no track qualifies.
